story.title: We All Must Compromise
paragraphs_en: Once upon a time, in a world very similar to ours, humans and animals lived in peace and harmony. Although they lived on the same planet, they managed to share their resources, not argue, and be kind to one another. All was well. Until one year, a very hot summer rolled around. In the town, there were two very popular restaurants. One of them was only for animals, called the Creature Café, and the other was only for humans, called the People Parlour. One sunny afternoon, a mother dog and her little puppy were going out for lunch, ready to eat a wonderful meal at the Creature Café, and this is where our story begins.

The two dogs took a seat inside the restaurant, near the window, wagging their tails and eagerly waiting for their waiter so that they could order their food. “Oh, I’m so hungry and thirsty! It’s such a hot day today! I think I’ll have at least five cups of water!” the puppy said with joy, dreaming about his upcoming meal. The mother dog chuckled. “There, there, we must be patient. I’m sure the waiter will be around quite soon,” she said, smiling at her son. The mother dog was right, because as soon as she said those words, the waiter rushed up to their table. “Hello! Welcome to Creature Café! My name is Zelly the Zebra, and I’ll be your waiter today! What can I get you?” Zelly asked, taking his notepad out. “Well, before we order our food, can we have two glasses of water, please?” the mother dog asked, holding up her empty glass. “We’re so thirsty, it’s such a hot day!”

Zelly the Zebra suddenly turned sad. “Oh, I’m so sorry, I’m afraid I won’t be able to serve you water today.” “No water?!” the puppy exclaimed. “But I’m so thirsty! Mommy, do something!” “Wait, but why can’t you serve us some water?” the mother dog asked the waiter, very confused. “Well, you see, People Parlour and Creature Café share the same water source. For the past month, People Parlour has been taking double of what they usually take, leaving Creature Café with close to nothing. I’m sorry, but I won’t be able to serve you water today,” Zelly the Zebra walked away sadly. “Wait, I’m confused,” the puppy said. “Why can’t we have any water just because People Parlour is taking more?”

“Well, you see, they are taking our share,” the mother dog explained.“The more water they take, the lesser we have.” “But that’s not fair!” the little puppy exclaimed. “We need water too! It’s not fair that the humans get all the water, this is our planet too!” “I know, and I agree,” the mother dog said solemnly. Then, she perked up. “Tell you what, how about you write them a letter?” she said excitedly, finding a paper napkin and a pen and handing it to her puppy. “Write down exactly what you told me and explain to them why they can’t take all the water.” “But they won’t listen to me.” the puppy said sadly. “I’m just a kid.” “That doesn’t mean you can’t make a change! You can do anything if you work hard. Try writing a letter, and let’s see what happens,” the mother dog said. “Okay, I’ll try!” the puppy squealed as he started writing the letter.

About a week later, the mother dog and her puppy made their way back to Creature Café. They sat at the same table and the same waiter came up to them. “Hello! Welcome to Creature Café! My name is Zelly the Zebra, and I’ll be your waiter today! What can I get you?” Zelly asked, taking his notepad out. “Zelly, do you have any water today? We really are very thirsty,” the mother dog pleaded, hoping against everything that there would be water for them to drink. Zelly the Zebra smiled a humongous smile. “As a matter of fact, we do! Your letter worked! The humans agreed to stop taking so much water, and we got our share back! Isn’t it wonderful?” He fetched a water pitcher from a counter in the restaurant and brought two empty glasses. He used the pitcher and poured water into each glass until they were each half full.

“Enjoy your water! I’ll be back in a few seconds,” Zelly the Zebra exclaimed as he went to tend to another customer. The puppy held the glass up in his hand, shocked. “Half a glass? I thought Zelly said my letter worked! Why do I only have half a glass?” The mother dog chuckled. “Well, we can’t have all the water, now can we? The humans need some too, don’t you think?” “But they took the water from us! We should be able to take it from them!” the puppy said. “Sweetheart, how did you feel when they took the water away from us?” the mother asked. “Sad,” the puppy muttered, looking down at the ground. “Well, how do you think they’ll feel if we take the water from them?” she asked.

The puppy looked up, realization dawning on his face. “I didn’t think of it that way. They’d be sad too. I don’t want them to be sad.” “I know you don’t.” she said. “That’s the thing. We all must compromise.” “Compro-what?” the puppy asked, not understanding the word. The mother dog laughed. “Compromise. It means that we need to learn to tend to other people’s needs too. We’re not the only ones who live on this planet, but all of us get everything we need from it. We need to learn to share. We might not always get what we want, but that means that we’re helping the humans get what they want too.”

“Oh, I get it! We share our resources and help each other live happy lives!” the puppy said happily, finally understanding. “Exactly! And the best part is that you don’t have to be an adult to understand that, or to make a change. Look at you! Your letter was what brought the water back to the restaurant. Age doesn’t matter. You have to believe that you can make a change. You can do anything if you believe in yourself.”

items.text_en: Once upon a time, in a world very similar to ours, humans and animals lived in peace and harmony.
Although they lived on the same planet, they managed to share their resources, not argue, and be kind to one another.
All was well.
Until one year, a very hot summer rolled around.
In the town, there were two very popular restaurants.
One of them was only for animals, called the Creature Café, and the other was only for humans, called the People Parlour.
One sunny afternoon, a mother dog and her little puppy were going out for lunch, ready to eat a wonderful meal at the Creature Café, and this is where our story begins.
The two dogs took a seat inside the restaurant, near the window, wagging their tails and eagerly waiting for their waiter so that they could order their food.
“Oh, I’m so hungry and thirsty!
It’s such a hot day today!
I think I’ll have at least five cups of water!” the puppy said with joy, dreaming about his upcoming meal.
The mother dog chuckled.
“There, there, we must be patient.
I’m sure the waiter will be around quite soon,” she said, smiling at her son.
The mother dog was right, because as soon as she said those words, the waiter rushed up to their table.
“Hello! Welcome to Creature Café!
My name is Zelly the Zebra, and I’ll be your waiter today!
What can I get you?” Zelly asked, taking his notepad out.
“Well, before we order our food, can we have two glasses of water, please?” the mother dog asked, holding up her empty glass.
“We’re so thirsty, it’s such a hot day!”
Zelly the Zebra suddenly turned sad.
“Oh, I’m so sorry, I’m afraid I won’t be able to serve you water today.” “No water?!” the puppy exclaimed.
“But I’m so thirsty!
Mommy, do something!” “Wait, but why can’t you serve us some water?” the mother dog asked the waiter, very confused.
“Well, you see, People Parlour and Creature Café share the same water source.
For the past month, People Parlour has been taking double of what they usually take, leaving Creature Café with close to nothing.
I’m sorry, but I won’t be able to serve you water today,” Zelly the Zebra walked away sadly.
“Wait, I’m confused,” the puppy said.
“Why can’t we have any water just because People Parlour is taking more?”
“Well, you see, they are taking our share,” the mother dog explained.“The more water they take, the lesser we have.” “But that’s not fair!” the little puppy exclaimed.
“We need water too!
It’s not fair that the humans get all the water, this is our planet too!” “I know, and I agree,” the mother dog said solemnly.
Then, she perked up.
“Tell you what, how about you write them a letter?” she said excitedly, finding a paper napkin and a pen and handing it to her puppy.
“Write down exactly what you told me and explain to them why they can’t take all the water.” “But they won’t listen to me.” the puppy said sadly.
“I’m just a kid.” “That doesn’t mean you can’t make a change!
You can do anything if you work hard.
Try writing a letter, and let’s see what happens,” the mother dog said.
“Okay, I’ll try!” the puppy squealed as he started writing the letter.
About a week later, the mother dog and her puppy made their way back to Creature Café.
They sat at the same table and the same waiter came up to them.
“Hello! Welcome to Creature Café!
My name is Zelly the Zebra, and I’ll be your waiter today!
What can I get you?” Zelly asked, taking his notepad out.
“Zelly, do you have any water today?
We really are very thirsty,” the mother dog pleaded, hoping against everything that there would be water for them to drink.
Zelly the Zebra smiled a humongous smile.
“As a matter of fact, we do!
Your letter worked!
The humans agreed to stop taking so much water, and we got our share back!
Isn’t it wonderful?” He fetched a water pitcher from a counter in the restaurant and brought two empty glasses.
He used the pitcher and poured water into each glass until they were each half full.
“Enjoy your water!
I’ll be back in a few seconds,” Zelly the Zebra exclaimed as he went to tend to another customer.
The puppy held the glass up in his hand, shocked.
“Half a glass?
I thought Zelly said my letter worked!
Why do I only have half a glass?” The mother dog chuckled.
“Well, we can’t have all the water, now can we?
The humans need some too, don’t you think?” “But they took the water from us!
We should be able to take it from them!” the puppy said.
“Sweetheart, how did you feel when they took the water away from us?” the mother asked.
“Sad,” the puppy muttered, looking down at the ground.
“Well, how do you think they’ll feel if we take the water from them?” she asked.
The puppy looked up, realization dawning on his face.
“I didn’t think of it that way.
They’d be sad too.
I don’t want them to be sad.” “I know you don’t.” she said.
“That’s the thing.
We all must compromise.” “Compro-what?” the puppy asked, not understanding the word.
The mother dog laughed.
“Compromise. It means that we need to learn to tend to other people’s needs too.
We’re not the only ones who live on this planet, but all of us get everything we need from it.
We need to learn to share.
We might not always get what we want, but that means that we’re helping the humans get what they want too.”
“Oh, I get it!
We share our resources and help each other live happy lives!” the puppy said happily, finally understanding.
“Exactly! And the best part is that you don’t have to be an adult to understand that, or to make a change.
Look at you!
Your letter was what brought the water back to the restaurant.
Age doesn’t matter.
You have to believe that you can make a change.
You can do anything if you believe in yourself.”
